# SharpCell.Grid

> A free (MIT) Excel-like spreadsheet control for .NET 8 and later, built on the SharpCell formula engine: it shows a worksheet the way Excel does, with number formats, cell styles, column widths, row heights, merged cells, frozen panes and text running on over empty cells. Only the visible cells are read, so any sheet size scrolls smoothly.

Packages: `SharpCell.Grid` (geometry, hit testing and painting, no UI framework), `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia` (`SpreadsheetView`, the Avalonia control) and `SharpCell.Grid.Wpf` (`SpreadsheetView` for WPF, Windows only). Namespaces: `SharpCell.Grid`, `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia`, `SharpCell.Grid.Wpf`; workbooks come from `SharpCell` and `SharpCell.Xlsx`. The view reads cells when it paints: after changing cells or recalculating, call `InvalidateVisual()`; after changing sizes or frozen panes, call `ReloadLayout()`. Cells are selected and copied as in Excel (`Selection`, `CopyAsync()`, `GridSelection`, `GridClipboard`); no editing yet.

---

<!-- page: index.md -->

# SharpCell.Grid

A free (MIT) Excel-like spreadsheet control for .NET 8 and later, built on the
[SharpCell](https://ifmelate.github.io/SharpCell/) formula engine. It shows a worksheet the way
Excel does: each cell's value in its number format and its style, the file's column widths and
row heights, merged cells, frozen panes and text running on over empty cells.

**[Try it in your browser](https://ifmelate.github.io/SharpCell.Grid/demo/)**: open your own .xlsx file; it is read on your computer and never uploaded.

![A sheet with styles, a merged title, wrapped text and a hidden column](images/styles.png)

| Package | What it does |
|---|---|
| `SharpCell.Grid` | Geometry, hit testing, scrolling and painting, with no UI framework. |
| `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia` | `SpreadsheetView`, the control for [Avalonia UI](https://avaloniaui.net). Brings `SharpCell.Grid` with it. |
| `SharpCell.Grid.Wpf` | `SpreadsheetView`, the same control for WPF on Windows. Brings `SharpCell.Grid` with it. |

Namespaces: `SharpCell`, `SharpCell.Xlsx` and `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia`.

```csharp snippet=show-workbook
Workbook workbook = XlsxReader.Load(path);
workbook.Recalculate();

var view = new SpreadsheetView { Worksheet = workbook["Budget"] };
```

Only the visible cells are read when the grid paints, so a sheet of a million rows scrolls like
an empty one. What a cell shows comes from SharpCell: `Cell.Text` for the value through its number
format, `Cell.Style` for the font, fill, borders and alignment. Both are checked against Microsoft
Excel.

Status: 0.x, viewing, selecting and copying, in Avalonia and WPF. Editing comes next; see the
[roadmap](roadmap.md). The API may change between minor versions until 1.0.

- [Getting started](getting-started.md)
- [What the grid shows](guides/showing-workbooks.md)
- [Painting in other UI frameworks](guides/painting.md)
- [API reference](api/index.md)

---

<!-- page: getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

## Install

```bash
dotnet add package SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia   # the control; brings SharpCell.Grid and SharpCell
dotnet add package SharpCell.Xlsx            # to read .xlsx files
```

The packages target .NET 8 and .NET 10 and Avalonia 12. For WPF, see [WPF](#wpf) below.

## Show a workbook

```csharp snippet=show-workbook
Workbook workbook = XlsxReader.Load(path);
workbook.Recalculate();

var view = new SpreadsheetView { Worksheet = workbook["Budget"] };
```

`SpreadsheetView` is an Avalonia control: put it in a window or any panel, and it takes the space
it is given. `XlsxReader.Load` reads values, formulas, the results Excel saved, number formats,
styles and the sheet's sizes; `Recalculate` calculates every formula with SharpCell.

A runnable window is in [samples/SharpCell.Grid.Sample](../samples/SharpCell.Grid.Sample):

```bash
dotnet run --project samples/SharpCell.Grid.Sample -f net10.0 -- path/to/file.xlsx
```

## After changes

```csharp snippet=refresh
sheet["B2"].Value = 99;
workbook.Recalculate();
view.InvalidateVisual();     // values, formulas and styles show at the next paint

sheet.SetColumnWidth(2, 20);
sheet.FrozenRows = 1;
view.ReloadLayout();         // sizes and frozen panes are taken again
```

The view reads cells each time it paints, but it does not know when a workbook changes. Column
widths, row heights, hidden rows and columns and frozen panes are taken when `Worksheet` is set,
and again with `ReloadLayout`.

## WPF

```bash
dotnet add package SharpCell.Grid.Wpf   # the WPF control; brings SharpCell.Grid and SharpCell
dotnet add package SharpCell.Xlsx
```

`SharpCell.Grid.Wpf` has the same `SpreadsheetView`, as a WPF `FrameworkElement` in the namespace
`SharpCell.Grid.Wpf`, for `net8.0-windows` and `net10.0-windows`. In XAML:

```xml
<Window xmlns:grid="clr-namespace:SharpCell.Grid.Wpf;assembly=SharpCell.Grid.Wpf" ...>
    <grid:SpreadsheetView x:Name="View" />
</Window>
```

```csharp snippet=show-workbook-wpf
Workbook workbook = XlsxReader.Load(path);
workbook.Recalculate();
View.Worksheet = workbook.Sheets[0];   // View: <grid:SpreadsheetView x:Name="View" /> in MainWindow.xaml
```

It shows, selects and copies as the Avalonia control does, and has the same properties: `Worksheet`,
`Selection`, `ActiveCell`, `Offset` (dependency properties), `Painter`, `ReloadLayout()`; copying
is `Copy()`, also bound to `ApplicationCommands.Copy`, and Ctrl+A to `ApplicationCommands.SelectAll`.
A runnable window is in [samples/SharpCell.Grid.WpfSample](../samples/SharpCell.Grid.WpfSample).

## Selection, copying and scrolling

```csharp snippet=active-cell
view.ActiveCell = new CellPosition(row: 10, column: 3);                // C10, selected alone
view.Selection = view.Selection!.Extend(rows: 2, columns: 1, sheet);   // C10:D12, as Shift with the arrows
view.Offset = new Vector(0, 200);                                      // scrolled ten default rows down
await view.CopyAsync();                                                // as Ctrl+C
```

`ActiveCell`, `Selection` and `Offset` are Avalonia properties, so they can be bound. The active
cell is the selection's; setting it selects that cell alone. Cells are selected with the mouse and
keyboard as in Excel, and copying puts them on the clipboard as text and as an HTML table, which
Excel pastes with their styles. The wheel scrolls three rows a turn.

---

<!-- page: guides/showing-workbooks.md -->

# What the grid shows

What a cell shows comes from SharpCell, and how the sheet is laid out follows Excel at 100% zoom.

## Values and number formats

Each cell shows `Cell.Text`: the value through its number format, with the workbook's culture.
Excel's General alignment puts numbers and dates on the right, text on the left, logical values
and errors in the middle.

A number too wide for its column is shortened as Excel does it: a number in the General format
loses decimals, rounding, or digits of its scientific notation; any other number shows `#` across
the cell. Text is never shortened.

## Styles

![Fonts, fills, borders, wrapped text and an indent](../images/styles.png)

`Cell.Style` gives the font (name, size, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, colour), the
fill, the four edges of the border and the alignment. Fills lie over the gridlines, as in Excel.
Wrapped text breaks onto more lines inside its cell; an indent moves text away from the edge it
is aligned to.

## Sizes and merged cells

Column widths and row heights come from the sheet, in pixels as Excel converts them: a width is
counted in digits of the workbook's default font, so it follows the font the grid measures with.
Hidden rows and columns take no space. A merged area shows its top-left cell across the whole
area; clicking anywhere in it selects that cell, and the arrow keys step over it as one cell.

## Running text

Text wider than its cell runs on over empty neighbours, away from the side it is aligned to: to
the right when left-aligned, to the left when right-aligned, both ways when centred. A cell with
content, a formula that gives empty text, or a merged area stops it. Numbers, wrapped text and
merged cells never run on.

## Frozen panes and gridlines

![Frozen rows and a frozen column, with gridlines turned off](../images/frozen.png)

Frozen rows and columns stay in place while the rest scrolls, with a line where they are frozen,
as Excel's Freeze Panes. A sheet with gridlines turned off shows none.

## Mouse and keyboard

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| Click on a cell | Selects it alone; inside a merged area, the area |
| Drag | Selects from where the drag started; past an edge of the view it scrolls after the mouse |
| Shift+click | Extends the selection from the active cell |
| Click or drag on column or row headers | Whole columns or rows; the active cell is the first on screen |
| Click on the corner above the row headers, Ctrl+A or Cmd+A | The whole sheet |
| Arrow keys | Move the active cell one cell, over a merged area as one cell, and select it alone |
| Shift+arrow keys | Extend or shrink the selection at its far corner |
| Ctrl+Space, Shift+Space | Whole columns, whole rows of the selection |
| Enter, Shift+Enter | Down, up; inside a selection, to the next selected cell, column by column |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Right, left; inside a selection, to the next selected cell, row by row |
| Ctrl+C or Cmd+C | Copies the selected cells; pasting into the grid comes with editing |
| Wheel | Three rows a turn |

A selection covers every merged area it touches whole. Selected cells but the active one are
shaded, a border goes round them, and the headers of their rows and columns are highlighted.

## Copying to Excel

Copying puts the selected cells on the clipboard in two forms, both read by Excel when it pastes:

- Text, as Excel copies it: a tab between cells, a line break after each row, text with line
  breaks in quotes. Other applications, such as editors and chat, take this form.
- An HTML table with each cell's font, fill, borders and alignment, and merged areas as one cell.
  Excel and other spreadsheets paste it with its styles; text stays text, even when it reads as a
  number.

Cells are copied as shown, in their number format: `1,250.00` rather than `1250`, and a formula's
value rather than the formula. Hidden rows and columns are copied. Whole columns or rows end at the
sheet's last used row or column.

## Where it differs from Excel

- Fonts the system does not have fall back to another font, so sizes follow the font that is used.
- Double underlines are drawn single; Fill, Justify and Distributed alignment are drawn as left or centred.
- Theme colours with a tint, indent steps and centred text blocked on one side follow the OOXML
  definitions; they are not yet compared with Excel.
- A merged area across the line of frozen panes is drawn whole from the frozen part.
- The colours of the selection, its shade and its headers are close to Excel's, not measured from it.
- Ctrl+A selects the whole sheet at once, not first the cells around the active one; Ctrl with the
  arrows, Home, Page Up and Page Down do not move yet, and only one rectangle can be selected
  (no Ctrl+click).
- Copied HTML is not yet checked by pasting it into desktop Excel.
- Not shown: conditional formats, pattern and gradient fills, rotated text, styles of whole rows
  and columns on empty cells, charts, images and comments.

---

<!-- page: guides/painting.md -->

# Painting in other UI frameworks

`SharpCell.Grid` holds everything about the grid that is not Avalonia or WPF: sizes and positions,
hit testing, selection, copying, scrolling and painting. The two `SpreadsheetView` controls are
thin hosts over it, and a host for another UI framework is the same few calls.

```csharp snippet=painter
var painter = new GridPainter
{
    // Text width in your UI framework's font engine, for fitting numbers and running text.
    MeasureText = (text, font) => text.Length * font.Size * 0.5,
};
painter.Layout = SheetLayout.FromWorksheet(sheet, painter.MaxDigitWidth(sheet));
painter.FrozenRows = sheet.FrozenRows;
painter.FrozenColumns = sheet.FrozenColumns;

var viewport = new GridViewport(OffsetX: 0, OffsetY: 0, Width: 800, Height: 600);
var selection = GridSelection.Cell(new CellPosition(1, 1), sheet);
painter.Paint(canvas, sheet, viewport, selection);   // canvas: your IGridCanvas

// A click, then a drag to (300, 90): what Excel selects, and what is copied.
if (painter.Hit(viewport, x: 120, y: 30, sheet) is { } hit)
    selection = GridSelection.At(hit, sheet).ExtendTo(painter.CellNearest(viewport, 300, 90), sheet);
string copied = GridClipboard.Text(sheet, selection.Area);
```

## The parts

- `SheetLayout` holds the column widths and row heights in pixels, their offsets, the cell under
  an offset and the cells in a rectangle. `SheetLayout.FromWorksheet` converts a sheet's sizes as
  Excel does, from the width of the widest digit of the default font.
- `GridViewport` is what is shown: the scroll offset into the sheet and the size of the grid on
  screen, headers included.
- `GridPainter` paints the part of the sheet in a viewport and the selection onto an `IGridCanvas`,
  and answers where a cell is (`CellBounds`), what is under a point (`HitTest` for cells, `Hit`
  for headers and the corner too), which cell a drag has reached (`CellNearest`, past the edges the
  next one out of view), and where to scroll (`ScrollIntoView`, `Clamp`).
- `GridSelection` is Excel's selection: what a click selects (`At`), and each step of the mouse
  and keyboard (`ExtendTo`, `Extend`, `Move`, `MoveWithin`, `EntireColumns`, `EntireRows`). A host
  maps its input events to these calls; `SpreadsheetView` shows how.
- `GridClipboard` gives the selected cells as text and as HTML, the forms Excel pastes, and
  `WindowsHtml` wraps the HTML in the clipboard format Windows applications read.
- `IGridCanvas` is what a host implements over its drawing API: fill and stroke rectangles, draw
  lines with a dash pattern, draw text inside bounds, cut off at them, on one line or wrapped.

## Measuring text

`GridPainter.MeasureText` gives the width of text in a font, from the host's font engine. With it,
numbers are fitted to their column, text runs on over empty cells, and row headers widen for long
row numbers. Without it, nothing is fitted and Calibri 11's digit width (7 pixels) is assumed.

`GridFont` sizes are in device-independent pixels: 11 points are 14.67 pixels at 96 DPI.
`GridPainter.FontOf` converts a SharpCell font.

---

<!-- page: roadmap.md -->

# Roadmap

Where SharpCell.Grid is going, in the order the work is planned. Each step ships when its tests
pass and what it shows is checked against Microsoft Excel. Dates are not promised; the project
has one maintainer.

## Released: 0.1 — a faithful viewer

A workbook from Excel looks the same in the grid as in Excel at 100% zoom.

| Step | What | Needs from SharpCell |
|---|---|---|
| Done | Headers, gridlines, `Cell.Text`, General alignment, active cell, mouse, arrows, Enter/Tab, wheel, numbers fitted to their column, row headers widened for long numbers | `Cell.Text` (0.5.0) |
| Done | Cell styles: fonts (name, size, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, colour), solid fills, borders, horizontal and vertical alignment, wrapped text, indent | `Cell.Style`, theme and indexed colours resolved (0.6.0) |
| Done | Sheet geometry from the file: column widths, row heights, hidden columns and rows | `Worksheet` column widths, row heights, hidden columns (0.6.0) |
| Done | Merged cells, painted and navigated as one cell | `Worksheet.MergedAreas` (0.6.0) |
| Done | Text running on over empty neighbours, by its alignment, also from cells out of view | — |
| Done | Frozen panes and the sheet's gridline setting | `Worksheet.FrozenRows`, `FrozenColumns`, `ShowGridlines` (0.6.0) |
| Done | A live demo in the browser through WebAssembly, on the documentation site | — |
| Released | 0.1.0 on NuGet: `SharpCell.Grid`, `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia` | SharpCell 0.6.0 |

## Now: 0.2 — selection and WPF

| Step | What | Needs from SharpCell |
|---|---|---|
| Done | Range selection: the mouse with dragging and Shift, Shift with the arrows, whole columns and rows from their headers and with Ctrl+Space and Shift+Space, the whole sheet; Enter and Tab inside a selection | — |
| Done | Copy as tab-separated text and as HTML with styles, values as shown | — |
| Done | A WPF control over the same painter: `SharpCell.Grid.Wpf`, tested on Windows in CI | — |

## Next: 0.3 — editing

- Typing into a cell and the formula bar as a separate control; F2, Escape, Enter, Tab.
- Input read as Excel reads it: numbers, percentages, dates and times in the workbook's culture,
  `=` for formulas, `'` for text.
- Recalculation after each edit, repainting only what changed (SharpCell's changed cells).
- Undo and redo, Delete, paste of values from Excel.
- Ctrl with the arrows, Home, Page Up and Page Down; Ctrl+A on the cells around the active one first.

## Later: 0.4 — working like Excel

- Resizing columns and rows with the mouse, double-click to fit.
- Inserting and deleting rows and columns, with formulas following (needs reference shifting in SharpCell).
- The fill handle for series and copied formulas.
- Zoom.
- Saving changed styles and geometry (needs the .xlsx writer in SharpCell to write styles).

## Quality, all along

- **Oracle for geometry and display:** desktop Excel exports `Range.Text`, `Left`, `Top`,
  `Width` and `Height` and `Range.Interior.Color` for test workbooks through SharpCell's
  `tools/excel-oracle`; the grid's numbers are compared with them. To be checked this way:
  the General shortening in narrow columns, theme colours with tints, indent steps and how
  centred text runs on when one side is blocked.
- **Snapshots** of rendered frames for every visible feature.
- **Benchmarks:** scrolling a million-row sheet, painting a full screen of styled cells.
- **NativeAOT and trimming** proved by a published smoke test, as in SharpCell.
- **Documentation site** with tested code snippets and `llms.txt`, as in SharpCell.

## Not planned

Charts, pivot tables, conditional formatting, data validation lists, comments, images and
macros. A workbook with them shows its cells; the rest is not drawn.

---

<!-- page: agents.md -->

# For AI coding agents

The documentation is published for agents as plain text:

- [llms.txt](https://ifmelate.github.io/SharpCell.Grid/llms.txt): an index of the pages with one line each.
- [llms-full.txt](https://ifmelate.github.io/SharpCell.Grid/llms-full.txt): all guides and the API reference in one file.

Every page of the site also has its Markdown source next to it.

## Rules to paste into an agent's instructions

```text
SharpCell.Grid shows SharpCell worksheets in Avalonia (SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia) or WPF (SharpCell.Grid.Wpf): new SpreadsheetView { Worksheet = sheet }.
The view reads cells when it paints: after changing cells or recalculating, call view.InvalidateVisual().
Sizes, hidden rows and columns and frozen panes are taken when Worksheet is set: after changing them, call view.ReloadLayout().
Rows and columns are numbered from 1: new CellPosition(row, column).
What a cell shows is SharpCell's Cell.Text and Cell.Style; change the workbook, not the view.
The selection is view.Selection, a GridSelection; view.ActiveCell is its active cell, and setting it selects that cell alone.
Copying (Avalonia: await view.CopyAsync(); WPF: view.Copy()) puts text and HTML for Excel on the clipboard; GridClipboard gives the same without a view.
The grid is for viewing and selecting; it does not edit cells yet.
For another UI framework, implement IGridCanvas and call GridPainter.Paint, Hit, CellNearest and ScrollIntoView, with GridSelection for the input.
```

A rectangle of cells, from its top-left to its bottom-right cell; rows and columns from 1.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.Grid.GridClipboard.md -->

# GridClipboard

```csharp
public static class GridClipboard
```

Namespace `SharpCell.Grid` · package `SharpCell.Grid`

What copying cells puts on the clipboard, in the forms Excel reads when it pastes: text with tabs between cells, and an HTML table that keeps fonts, fills, borders, alignment and merged cells. Cells are copied as shown, `Cell.Text` in their number format. Hidden rows and columns are copied, as Excel copies them. Whole columns or rows end at the sheet's used range.

## Methods

<a id="html-worksheet-cellarea"></a>
### Html(Worksheet, CellArea)

```csharp
public static string Html(Worksheet sheet, CellArea area)
```

The cells as an HTML document with one table, whose cells carry their style inline and merged areas as `colspan` and `rowspan`; the table lies between the `<!--StartFragment-->` and `<!--EndFragment-->` comments. On macOS and Linux it goes on the clipboard as it is; Windows needs it wrapped by [GridClipboard.WindowsHtml](SharpCell.Grid.GridClipboard.md#windowshtml-string).

<a id="text-worksheet-cellarea"></a>
### Text(Worksheet, CellArea)

```csharp
public static string Text(Worksheet sheet, CellArea area)
```

The cells as text, as Excel puts them on the clipboard: a tab between cells, a line break after each row, the last one too. Text with a line break or a tab is put in double quotes, with any quote inside doubled.

<a id="windowshtml-string"></a>
### WindowsHtml(string)

```csharp
public static string WindowsHtml(string html)
```

HTML in the clipboard format Windows applications read, `HTML Format`: a header giving where the document and its fragment start and end, as byte offsets into its UTF-8 encoding, then the document. Put it on the clipboard as UTF-8 bytes.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The document has no `<!--StartFragment-->` and `<!--EndFragment-->` comments.

|---|---|---|

| <a id="dash"></a>`Dash` | 1 | Dashes. |
| <a id="dot"></a>`Dot` | 2 | Dots. |

# GridFont

```csharp

```

Namespace `SharpCell.Grid` · package `SharpCell.Grid`

A font to draw text with; the size is in pixels, not points.

## Constructors

### GridFont(string, double, bool, bool, bool, bool)

```csharp
public GridFont(string Family, double Size, bool Bold = false, bool Italic = false, bool Underline = false, bool Strikethrough = false)
```

A font to draw text with; the size is in pixels, not points.

**Parameters**

- `Family`: The font family, such as `Calibri`; a canvas falls back to its own font when the family is missing.
- `Size`: The size in device-independent pixels: 11 points are 14.67 pixels at 96 DPI.
- `Bold`: Bold text.
- `Italic`: Italic text.
- `Underline`: Underlined text.
- `Strikethrough`: Text struck through.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.Grid.GridPainter.md -->

# GridPainter

```csharp
public sealed class GridPainter
```

Namespace `SharpCell.Grid` · package `SharpCell.Grid`

Paints a worksheet the way Excel shows it: column and row headers, gridlines, each cell's `Cell.Text` in its style (font, fill, borders, alignment, wrapping, indent), merged areas as one cell, and the active cell. Only the cells inside the viewport are read, so a sheet's size does not matter. Also answers the geometry questions of a grid on screen: where a cell is, what is under a point, where to scroll. With [GridPainter.MeasureText](SharpCell.Grid.GridPainter.md#measuretext) set, text too wide for its cell runs on over empty neighbours, numbers too wide for their column are shortened or shown as `###`, and row headers widen for long row numbers, as in Excel.

## Constructors

<a id="ctor"></a>
### GridPainter()

```csharp
public GridPainter()
```

A painter with Excel's default row heights and column widths.

<a id="ctor-sheetlayout"></a>
### GridPainter(SheetLayout)

```csharp
public GridPainter(SheetLayout layout)
```

A painter over the given sizes of rows and columns.

## Properties

<a id="columnheaderheight"></a>
### ColumnHeaderHeight

```csharp
public double ColumnHeaderHeight { get; set; }
```

The height of the column headers at the top.

<a id="frozencolumns"></a>
### FrozenColumns

```csharp
public int FrozenColumns { get; set; }
```

How many columns on the left stay in place while the rest scrolls; a sheet's own is `Worksheet.FrozenColumns`.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The count is negative or leaves no column to scroll.

<a id="frozenrows"></a>
### FrozenRows

```csharp
public int FrozenRows { get; set; }
```

How many rows at the top stay in place while the rest scrolls, as Excel's Freeze Panes; a sheet's own is `Worksheet.FrozenRows`.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The count is negative or leaves no row to scroll.

<a id="layout"></a>
### Layout

```csharp
public SheetLayout Layout { get; set; }
```

The sizes of rows and columns; [SheetLayout.FromWorksheet](SharpCell.Grid.SheetLayout.md#fromworksheet-worksheet-double) gives a sheet's own.

<a id="measuretext"></a>
### MeasureText

```csharp
public Func<string, GridFont, double>? MeasureText { get; set; }
```

The width in pixels of a line of text in a font. Without it, text is never fitted to its cell, row headers keep [GridPainter.RowHeaderWidth](SharpCell.Grid.GridPainter.md#rowheaderwidth), and Calibri 11's digit width is assumed.

<a id="rowheaderwidth"></a>
### RowHeaderWidth

```csharp
public double RowHeaderWidth { get; set; }
```

The width of the row headers on the left; with [GridPainter.MeasureText](SharpCell.Grid.GridPainter.md#measuretext), the least width, widened to fit the number of the last visible row.

<a id="theme"></a>
### Theme

```csharp
public GridTheme Theme { get; set; }
```

The colours of everything but the cells' own styles.

## Methods

What is under a point of the grid: a cell, a column or row header, or the corner above the row headers; null outside the grid. [GridSelection.At](SharpCell.Grid.GridSelection.md#at-gridhit-worksheet) turns it into what a click selects.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.Grid.GridSelection.md -->

# GridSelection

```csharp
public sealed class GridSelection
```

Namespace `SharpCell.Grid` · package `SharpCell.Grid`

The selected cells, as in Excel: a rectangle of cells and the active cell inside it. The rectangle runs from the [GridSelection.Anchor](SharpCell.Grid.GridSelection.md#anchor), where the selection started, to the [GridSelection.Extent](SharpCell.Grid.GridSelection.md#extent), the corner the mouse or Shift with the arrows moves, and grows to cover whole every merged area it touches. Whole columns span every row of the sheet, whole rows every column. A selection never changes; each step gives a new one.

## Properties

<a id="activecell"></a>
### ActiveCell

```csharp
public CellPosition ActiveCell { get; }
```

The cell typing would go into, with the white background inside the shaded selection.

<a id="anchor"></a>
### Anchor

```csharp
public CellPosition Anchor { get; }
```

The corner the selection started from; it stays when the selection is extended.

<a id="area"></a>
### Area

```csharp
public CellArea Area { get; }
```

The selected cells, merged areas they touch included.

<a id="extent"></a>
### Extent

```csharp
public CellPosition Extent { get; }
```

The corner opposite the anchor, which extending the selection moves.

<a id="isentirecolumns"></a>
### IsEntireColumns

```csharp
public bool IsEntireColumns { get; }
```

Whether the selection spans every row: whole columns, or the whole sheet.

<a id="isentirerows"></a>
### IsEntireRows

```csharp
public bool IsEntireRows { get; }
```

Whether the selection spans every column: whole rows, or the whole sheet.

<a id="issinglecell"></a>
### IsSingleCell

```csharp
public bool IsSingleCell { get; }
```

Whether only the active cell is selected; a merged area counts as one cell.

## Methods

<a id="all-cellposition"></a>
### All(CellPosition)

```csharp
public static GridSelection All(CellPosition activeCell)
```

The whole sheet, keeping the active cell where it is.

<a id="at-gridhit-worksheet"></a>
### At(GridHit, Worksheet)

```csharp
public static GridSelection At(GridHit hit, Worksheet? sheet)
```

What a click selects: a cell, whole columns from a column header, whole rows from a row header, the whole sheet from the corner above the row headers.

<a id="cell-cellposition-worksheet"></a>
### Cell(CellPosition, Worksheet)

```csharp
public static GridSelection Cell(CellPosition cell, Worksheet? sheet)
```

One cell, or the merged area holding it.

<a id="columns-int-int-int-worksheet"></a>
### Columns(int, int, int, Worksheet)

```csharp
public static GridSelection Columns(int first, int last, int activeRow, Worksheet? sheet)
```

Whole columns, from the first to the last, with the active cell in the first column.

**Parameters**

- `first`: The column the selection starts from.
- `last`: The column it extends to; before `first` for a selection extended to the left.
- `activeRow`: The row of the active cell: in Excel, the top row on screen.
- `sheet`: The sheet, whose merged areas the selection covers whole.

<a id="contains-int-int"></a>
### Contains(int, int)

```csharp
public bool Contains(int row, int column)
```

Whether a cell is selected.

<a id="entirecolumns-worksheet"></a>


<a id="entirerows-worksheet"></a>

```csharp
public GridSelection EntireRows(Worksheet? sheet)
```

Whole rows under the selection, keeping the active cell, as Shift+Space does.

<a id="extend-int-int-worksheet"></a>
### Extend(int, int, Worksheet)

```csharp
public GridSelection Extend(int rows, int columns, Worksheet? sheet)
```

The selection grown or shrunk by whole rows and columns at its extent, as Shift with the arrows does; a step that a merged area swallows goes on until the selection changes.

<a id="extendto-cellposition-worksheet"></a>
### ExtendTo(CellPosition, Worksheet)

```csharp
public GridSelection ExtendTo(CellPosition cell, Worksheet? sheet)
```

The selection from the same anchor to a cell, as when dragging the mouse or Shift-clicking: whole columns or rows stay whole, the active cell stays.

<a id="extendto-gridhit-worksheet"></a>
### ExtendTo(GridHit, Worksheet)

```csharp
public GridSelection ExtendTo(GridHit hit, Worksheet? sheet)
```

The selection from the same anchor to what a Shift-click hits: to a cell, to whole columns from a column header, to whole rows from a row header, the whole sheet from the corner.

<a id="move-int-int-worksheet"></a>
### Move(int, int, Worksheet)

```csharp
public GridSelection Move(int rows, int columns, Worksheet? sheet)
```

The active cell moved by whole rows and columns, as the arrows move it, and selected alone.

<a id="movewithin-int-int-worksheet"></a>
### MoveWithin(int, int, Worksheet)

```csharp
public GridSelection MoveWithin(int rows, int columns, Worksheet? sheet)
```

The active cell moved as Enter and Tab move it. A single cell moves as with the arrows; inside a larger selection it moves to the next cell of the selection, which stays, and wraps around: Enter goes down each column in turn, Tab across each row. Hidden cells and the inner cells of merged areas are passed over.

**Parameters**

- `rows`: 1 for Enter, -1 for Shift+Enter, 0 for Tab.
- `columns`: 1 for Tab, -1 for Shift+Tab, 0 for Enter.
- `sheet`: The sheet, whose hidden rows and columns and merged areas are passed over.

<a id="rows-int-int-int-worksheet"></a>
### Rows(int, int, int, Worksheet)

```csharp
public static GridSelection Rows(int first, int last, int activeColumn, Worksheet? sheet)
```

Whole rows, from the first to the last, with the active cell in the first row.

**Parameters**

- `first`: The row the selection starts from.
- `last`: The row it extends to; above `first` for a selection extended upwards.
- `activeColumn`: The column of the active cell: in Excel, the leftmost column on screen.
- `sheet`: The sheet, whose merged areas the selection covers whole.

<a id="tostring"></a>
### ToString()

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

The selected cells' address: `B3`, `B3:D7`, `C:E` for whole columns, `2:4` for whole rows.

# SheetLayout

```csharp
public sealed class SheetLayout
```

Namespace `SharpCell.Grid` · package `SharpCell.Grid`

Where the cells of a sheet are, in device-independent pixels from the top-left corner of cell A1: column widths, row heights, their offsets, the cell under a point and the cells inside a viewport. Covers Excel's whole sheet, 1,048,576 rows by 16,384 columns. Rows and columns are numbered from 1.

## Constructors




**Exceptions**

```csharp
public double Height { get; }
```

The height of all rows together.

<a id="width"></a>

```csharp

```

The width of all columns together.

## Methods


The width of a column.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The column is outside the sheet.

<a id="fromworksheet-worksheet-double"></a>
### FromWorksheet(Worksheet, double)

```csharp
public static SheetLayout FromWorksheet(Worksheet sheet, double maxDigitWidth)
```

A layout with a worksheet's column widths, row heights and hidden rows and columns, in pixels at 100% zoom as Excel converts them: a width of `w` characters is `Truncate((256 * w + Truncate(128 / d)) / 256 * d)` pixels, `d` being the width of the widest digit of the workbook's default font (7 for Calibri 11); a height of `h` points is `h * 96 / 72` pixels, rounded. Later changes to the sheet are not followed.

**Parameters**

- `sheet`: The sheet.
- `maxDigitWidth`: The width in pixels of the widest digit of the default font.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The digit width is not positive.

<a id="rowat-double"></a>
### RowAt(double)

```csharp
public int RowAt(double y)
```

The row under a vertical offset, clamped to the sheet; hidden rows are never hit.

<a id="rowheight-int"></a>
### RowHeight(int)

```csharp
public double RowHeight(int row)
```

The height of a row.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The row is outside the sheet.

<a id="rowtop-int"></a>
### RowTop(int)

```csharp
public double RowTop(int row)
```

The offset of a row's top edge; 0 for row 1.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The row is outside the sheet.

<a id="setcolumnwidth-int-double"></a>
### SetColumnWidth(int, double)

```csharp
public void SetColumnWidth(int column, double width)
```

Gives a column a width; zero hides it, the default width forgets the change.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The column is outside the sheet, or the width is negative.

<a id="setrowheight-int-double"></a>
### SetRowHeight(int, double)

```csharp
public void SetRowHeight(int row, double height)
```

Gives a row a height; zero hides it, the default height forgets the change.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The row is outside the sheet, or the height is negative.

<a id="visiblearea-double-double-double-double"></a>
### VisibleArea(double, double, double, double)

```csharp
public CellArea VisibleArea(double x, double y, double width, double height)
```

The cells that a rectangle of the sheet touches, partly or wholly.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The width or height is negative.

<!-- page: api/SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia.SpreadsheetView.md -->

# SpreadsheetView

```csharp
public class SpreadsheetView : Control
```

Namespace `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia` · package `SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia`

Shows a SharpCell worksheet as Excel does: headers, gridlines, each cell's text as Excel formats it in the cell's style, the sheet's column widths, row heights, merged cells, frozen panes and gridlines. Cells are selected as in Excel: by clicking and dragging, by Shift with a click or the arrows, whole columns and rows from their headers or with Ctrl+Space and Shift+Space, the whole sheet from the corner or with Ctrl+A or Cmd+A. Enter and Tab move inside a selection, the wheel scrolls, and Ctrl+C or Cmd+C puts the selected cells on the clipboard as Excel pastes them. Only the visible cells are read, so any sheet size works. The view reads cells when it paints; after changing cells or recalculating, call `Visual.InvalidateVisual`. Sizes and frozen panes are taken when [SpreadsheetView.Worksheet](SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia.SpreadsheetView.md#worksheet) is set; after changing them, call [SpreadsheetView.ReloadLayout](SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia.SpreadsheetView.md#reloadlayout).

## Constructors

<a id="ctor"></a>
### SpreadsheetView()

```csharp
public SpreadsheetView()
```

Creates an empty view; set [SpreadsheetView.Worksheet](SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia.SpreadsheetView.md#worksheet) to show a sheet.

## Properties

<a id="activecell"></a>
### ActiveCell

```csharp
public CellPosition? ActiveCell { get; set; }
```

The cell with the active-cell border; null shows none. It is the active cell of [SpreadsheetView.Selection](SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia.SpreadsheetView.md#selection); setting it selects that cell alone.

<a id="offset"></a>
### Offset

```csharp
public Vector Offset { get; set; }
```

How far the cells are scrolled, in pixels from cell A1; kept inside the sheet when painting.

<a id="painter"></a>
### Painter

```csharp
public GridPainter Painter { get; }
```

Geometry and colours: row heights, column widths, header sizes, theme.

<a id="selection"></a>
### Selection

```csharp
public GridSelection? Selection { get; set; }
```

The selected cells, the active cell among them; null selects none. A new sheet starts from its active cell alone.

<a id="viewport"></a>
### Viewport

```csharp
public GridViewport Viewport { get; }
```

What the view shows now: its size and its offset, kept inside the sheet.

<a id="worksheet"></a>
### Worksheet

```csharp
public Worksheet? Worksheet { get; set; }
```

The sheet shown; null shows an empty grid.

## Methods

<a id="copyasync"></a>
### CopyAsync()

```csharp
public Task CopyAsync()
```

Puts the selected cells on the clipboard as Excel pastes them: as text with tabs between cells, and as an HTML table with their styles. Ctrl+C or Cmd+C does it too, also in a browser.

<a id="reloadlayout"></a>
### ReloadLayout()

```csharp
public void ReloadLayout()
```

Takes the sheet's column widths, row heights, hidden rows and columns and frozen panes again.

<a id="render-drawingcontext"></a>
### Render(DrawingContext)

```csharp
public override void Render(DrawingContext context)
```

Paints the visible part of the sheet through [SpreadsheetView.Painter](SharpCell.Grid.Avalonia.SpreadsheetView.md#painter).

**Parameters**

- `context`: The drawing context Avalonia renders with.

---
